rounds.proof_sketch: Original: grid_size=129, total_threads=33024, threads_per_channel=33024/1024=32. Mutated: grid_size=128, total_threads=32768, threads_per_channel=32768/1024=32. Since threads_per_channel is identical (32), work distribution is identical. The 256 excess threads in original would fail batch_channel>=1024 check anyway.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation subtracts 1 from the grid size, reducing total threads from 33024 to 32768. However, the threads_per_channel calculation (integer division by batch_size*channels=1024) yields 32 in both cases. With 1024 batch-channels each assigned exactly 32 threads, all output positions are covered by both versions. The extra 256 threads in the original kernel would have early-exited due to the batch_channel bounds check. The mutation removes only these ineffective threads.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutation removes only excess threads that were already returning early without contributing to the output.
rounds.recommendations: When testing launch configuration mutations, verify whether the mutation affects the actual work distribution (threads_per_channel, work items per thread) rather than just total thread count. Excess threads beyond the required work items do not affect correctness.
